MIT-WPU students design algae-based cooling façade
stories.summary: Students from MIT-WPU have developed a living façade using algae, cyanobacteria and moss to explore passive cooling for Indian buildings. The project won the Youth for Earth Campaign 2026, organised by the Mobius Foundation and The Climate Reality Project. The building is now expected to breathe.

stories.title: El Niño impact on Bharat monsoon patterns
stories.summary: The Ministry of Earth Sciences reports that nearly 44% of El Niño years have resulted in below-normal monsoons or severe droughts in Bharat. With the Southwest Monsoon supplying over 70% of the country's annual rainfall, the shifting Walker Circulation remains a significant variable for national water security.

stories.title: Bend Central Library receives LEED Platinum certification
stories.summary: The Central Library in Bend, Oregon, has earned LEED Platinum status for its sustainable design. The building is 100% solar-powered and features furniture made from sustainable forests without the use of glue. The Redmond Library has also received the same designation.

stories.title: Lagos school wins environmental prize
stories.summary: Slum2School Green Academy in Epe, Lagos, has won the 2026 World's Best School Prize for Environmental Action. The school provides education to 250 children from riverine communities, overcoming previous barriers to access caused by long canoe journeys. The prize recognises its solar, water and waste systems.

stories.title: RIBA reflects on COP31 climate presence
stories.summary: The Royal Institute of British Architects continues its annual attendance at COP summits to advocate for sustainable construction. With buildings accounting for 37% of global energy-related carbon emissions, the organisation maintains that architects must act as thought leaders in the ongoing global climate conversation.

stories.title: World Economic Forum ranks LC3 cement as top emerging technology
stories.summary: A cement blend using calcined clay and limestone, known as LC3, has been ranked first in a World Economic Forum report on technologies for planetary health. Developed by scientists from Cuba, Switzerland and India, the innovation is already being implemented in several countries.

stories.title: Indore university named World Building of the Year
stories.summary: The Prestige University in Indore has been named World Building of the Year at the 2026 World Architecture Festival. Designed by Sanjay Puri Architects, the structure features stepped forms inspired by 1,100-year-old Indian wells. It provides seating for 9,000 students across its 32-acre campus.

stories.title: Josephine Estate in Goa restored for modern living
stories.summary: The Portuguese villa Josephine Estate has been restored by Isprava to bridge the gap between architectural heritage and contemporary coastal living. The project preserved the original name inscribed on a handcrafted ceramic tile, envisioning the renovation as a dialogue between history and modern requirements.

stories.title: Sustainable home built around nature in Yercaud
stories.summary: Whispers of the Wild, a residential project by MAWI Design in Yercaud, features a stream flowing beneath a glass floor and a tree framed by glass walls. The architect states the most interesting aspect of the home is the landscape they chose not to remove.

stories.title: Aashish Vaishnava wins global golf design award
stories.summary: Aashish Vaishnava has become the first Indian golf course architect to win the World Golf Awards' Golf Course Designer of the Year title. Sharing the 2026 award with Jon Hunt, Vaishnava joins a list of previous winners that includes Jack Nicklaus and Greg Norman.

stories.title: Temple construction drives interest in traditional architecture
stories.summary: Renowned architect D N V Prasad Sthapathy reports that the current boom in temple construction is creating career opportunities for trained artisans and architects. Over 200 students are now pursuing specialised courses in traditional Indian temple architecture to meet the growing demand for skilled practitioners.

stories.title: Design vision unveiled for Mumbai cruise terminal
stories.summary: Rahul Mehta Architects has unveiled plans for the Mumbai International Cruise Terminal at Indira Dock. Developed under a public-private partnership with the Mumbai Port Authority, the terminal aims to integrate international cruise operations with retail and public spaces to extend the waterfront's utility.

stories.title: Tipu Sultan's palace survives as school
stories.summary: A structure believed to be Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace in Mysuru currently houses the Government Urdu Higher Primary Boys' School. Despite demolition attempts in 1992 and 2003, the surviving portion remains in use. The building serves as a reminder of its former royal purpose.

stories.title: ZHA completes theatre project in Morocco
stories.summary: ZHA has completed the Théâtre Royal de Rabat, the studio's first project in Africa. Located between Rabat and Salé, the building features three performance spaces and an exterior inspired by the riverbank site. The late Zaha Hadid originally described the design as secular.

Aga Khan Award evaluations prioritize cultural continuity in industrial heritage
stories.summary: A qualitative study published in the Journal of Umm Al-Qura University for Engineering and Architecture finds that Aga Khan Award jury evaluations prioritize community-driven socio-cultural continuity over technological novelty. The research examines how award frameworks apply adaptive reuse criteria to industrial sites. Continuity is the new innovation.

stories.title: Ten EU countries push to exclude Russia from 2027 Venice Biennale
stories.summary: Ten European Union countries have urged the European Commission to bar Russia from the 2027 Venice architecture biennale. The coalition, led by Poland, argues that participation normalizes Russia's actions in Ukraine. Russia participated in this year's event despite similar protests from several member states.

stories.title: Steel Architectural Awards ASEAN 2026 names four winners
stories.summary: Four projects were selected from 138 submissions as winners of the Steel Architectural Awards ASEAN 2026 in Bangkok. The biennial programme, presented by BlueScope, celebrates the use of coated steel in climate-responsive designs. The event also marked 60 years of the company's steel brand.

stories.title: Six Australian projects win at World Architecture Festival 2026
stories.summary: Australian architects secured six wins at the World Architecture Festival 2026. The event featured various industry updates, including construction progress on the Alice Springs Multicultural Centre and a design manual release. The festival remains a significant gathering for international architectural recognition.

stories.title: World Architecture Festival 2026 announces top global winners
stories.summary: Sanjay Puri Architects won World Building of the Year for a project in Indore, while &Matcha Three Yards in the Philippines was named World Interior of the Year. The interior project uses a 100-square-meter space to provide ecological repair. Gaps are now a design feature.

stories.title: Kathmandu hosts international architectural symposium Pathfinder 2026
stories.summary: Kathmandu is hosting the Pathfinder 2026 architectural symposium this evening. The event features international speakers, including former Sagrada Família technical office staff, to discuss design and materials with local academics. Organizers confirmed that all international guests have arrived in the capital for the exchange.

stories.title: Hempcrete gains official recognition in U.S. building codes
stories.summary: Hempcrete is now included in the 2024 International Residential Code, offering insulation and carbon storage benefits. While the material has gained federal recognition, individual cities and counties must still approve its use before builders can bypass special permits. Local adoption remains a separate process.

stories.title: Regolith bricks proposed for lunar construction
stories.summary: Establishing a permanent lunar base is a goal for future Mars missions, with regolith identified as a potential source for fuel and building materials. Transporting supplies from Earth is considered expensive and challenging. Bricks made from lunar dust are being evaluated as a local alternative.

Procurement teams are shifting toward certified isocyanate-free options to align with green building standards. Compliance is now a primary market driver.

stories.title: India expands geothermal energy exploration
stories.summary: India is increasing efforts to tap geothermal resources to diversify its renewable energy mix and reach Net Zero emissions by 2070. The country aims to translate resource assessments into practical power generation. Geothermal is being positioned as a reliable, round-the-clock source of clean energy.

stories.title: NHAI engineer identifies causes of early highway bridge deterioration
stories.summary: A senior NHAI engineer reports that neglect of small components like bearings and expansion joints is causing early deterioration in bridges designed for 100-year lifespans. The findings were presented at the Indian Roads Congress. Maintenance is often overlooked in favor of initial construction.

The centre will combine Autodesk’s cloud-based Forma platform with Neilsoft’s engineering and digital twin capabilities. The built environment is being transformed.

stories.summary: Autodesk and Neilsoft have sealed a deal to establish an AECO Centre of Excellence in Pune to accelerate the adoption of BIM, digital twin and AI-powered technologies. stories.summary: Researchers from QuEra Computing, NVIDIA, École Normale Supérieure and the University of Massachusetts Amherst have released the Programmable Pauli Virtual Machine. The open-source framework is designed to emulate quantum processors, hardware noise and classical control logic. It uses a virtual machine to separate a virtual CPU from a QPU.

The study, published in Applied Intelligence, suggests that incorporating AI assessments into group decisions can streamline the coordination of complex building projects.

The city is changing the way a modern city works.

stories.summary: Virginia Commonwealth University School of the Arts in Qatar will showcase bamboo-based designs at the Heenat Salma Farm Winter Bazaar from November 25 to 30. The exhibition features work from 27 senior students and 11 alumni. It explores how traditional materials can inform sustainable construction practices.

The challenge seeks designs that support human health and wellbeing by considering how light, sound and form affect the brain. The winning proposal receives $50,000.

stories.summary: Denver is using its landmark designation process to protect historic brick elementary schools. The city notes that these buildings, often featuring arched entryways and ornate details, shape how students focus and belong. The buildings are being preserved for their architecture and their role in city life.

stories.summary: Noriyuki Abe, the director behind Bleach and Yu Yu Hakusho, attended the debut of Anime India in Hyderabad. Abe, who studied architecture before entering the film industry, participated in fireside chats and met with fans. The event marked the director's first appearance at the convention.

stories.summary: Elizabeth Diller is designing the new MIT School of Architecture and Planning within the former Metropolitan Storage Warehouse. Diller aims to keep the building's history alive by exposing its original structure rather than covering it. She argues that buildings carry memories that are lost when they are demolished.
